findings.where: The pad ground across the whole page at both widths: the ruled lines and the double margin line down the left. The texture swatch is the only place they show in their stated colours
findings.fault: The direction calls for pale blue rules and a double red margin line, and the palette itself names Feint #93B3D3 for the rules and Margin red for the margin. On the page, though, both draw as dull olive-brown lines. Only the small texture swatch shows the blue feints. The page's main surface therefore contradicts its own palette, and it reads as khaki-ruled notepaper, not a canary legal pad. The red margin line, the mark that makes a legal pad, is lost.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who chose the legal pad 'given my legal background' and will judge the direction on whether it looks like one. The layout round would also object, because it would be building from swatches that the tile's own ground does not use.

findings.where: The nav bar (the binding strip), at both widths: the logo mark and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured pale yellow to sit on the dark binding red. The logo's own blue (#0070C0) and grey (#404040) appear nowhere on the page. The palette neither gives them a job nor declares them logo-only, so the site's identity has no link to the logo it must keep. Mark does not hold a yellow version of his logo.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo stays as it is and is built by the opening animation. A visitor who knows the blue wordmark would also object, since they lose the link between this site and his existing materials.

findings.where: The article specimen: the lecture/PDF attachment row ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'), at both widths
findings.fault: Two dark ink rules frame the row, and they are laid over paper that is already ruled. The bottom rule runs along the text baseline, so the title and the date/PDF label both look underlined. It reads as a dark divider fighting the feints, not a quiet grouping line.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page. The date and the 'PDF' label look as if they can be clicked, and the row looks crossed out more than set apart. Angélique would also object, because this is the treatment every PDF she adds would inherit.

findings.where: The palette tokens Ballpoint #1B2A6B (type) and Light hand #34407A (asides), as rendered in the hero's italic line 'Over 40 years…' and the article's byline
findings.fault: The two inks are close enough to read as one navy, so the 'asides' colour adds no visible distinction. It looks more like an accidental second token than a deliberate secondary ink.
findings.who_objects: The layout round and Angélique, who would have two near-identical text colours to choose between with no visible reason to pick either.
